key_insight: Severe plastic deformation of CrMnFeCoNi increases both electrical and thermal conductivity despite introducing defects, with inferred phonon transport rising far more than electron transport.
engineering_relevance: Defect and nanostructure engineering may enable high-entropy alloys that combine increased hardness with improved electrical and thermal transport.
method: Apply high-pressure torsion for up to 4 turns to generate hierarchical defects and grain refinement.
Evaluate hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity, heat capacity, and thermal expansion.
Use Wiedemann–Franz analysis and the Cahill–Pohl model to assess electron and phonon transport.
evidence_signal: After 4 turns, electrical conductivity rises from 0.953 to 1.003 ± 0.005 MS/m and thermal conductivity from 10.3 to 14.4 W/(m·K), while hardness saturates near 520 Hv.
watch_item: Deformation-induced short-range ordering is a proposed explanation, not a demonstrated mechanism; the phonon contribution is inferred through transport modeling.
paper_title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
